id: Bike Maintenance for Beginners-Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki St, Wellington-Event Finder
name: Bike Maintenance for Beginners
venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki St, Wellington
long_description:
Gain the confidence and skills to maintain your bicycle in good working order, and to diagnose and fix some mechanical problems. Get familiar with bike terms and tools and learn through practical experience.

Have you recently started riding a bike and want to make sure you can take care of it properly? Or have you been riding for ages, but have always been scared to fix anything yourself?

Are you unsure of how to pump your tyres, or how much oil your chain needs? Find yourself fumbling for words when trying to describe that clunking sound to the guy in the bike shop?

This one day course lays bare the nuts and bolts of bicycle mechanics for absolute beginners, as well as those with a little experience. Through practical experience working with your own bicycle, you will find out what needs to be done to keep it running smoothly. We’ll cover what to look out for when things start to wear out, and how to check for problems, so you can be confident your bicycle is safe to ride. You will also learn how to fix some of the most common mechanical problems, and learn about the correct terminology and tools to use.

Those who feel intimidated in bike shops are especially welcome in this course. No question is a stupid question!

Bringing a bike to work on is essential, preferably one that you are riding regularly, because the best way to learn is by building familiarity with your own ride. E-bikes are welcome, although the extra weight can mean they are more challenging to work on. Regardless of whether your bike is in pristine condition, or desperately in need of TLC, it is welcome on the course – bikes showing a bit more wear can be useful for the learning of the whole group.

Bring your pushbike along on the day, If you have the following, please bring them as well: A multi-tool and pump; chain oil and rag; lightweight close-fitting gardening or rubber gloves.

(Please note this course is not exhaustive and is not a professional training course).

By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
- Name most parts of a bicycle correctly
- Perform a quick safety check on any bicycle
- Fix a flat tyre
- Adjust your bike to fit your body
- Oil and clean your chain
- Identify and fix some common brake problems

Note: Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

long_description:

name: French Pastry for Beginners
venue: Le Ciel Bakery, 100 Tory Street, Te Aro, Wellington
long_description:
French Pastry for Beginners
A 4-Week Hands-On Series

Step into the world of French pâtisserie with our beginner-friendly four-week course designed to teach you the essential techniques behind some of France's most iconic pastries. Guided by Le Ciel's experienced pastry chef and owner, Shuchi, you'll build your confidence week by week as you learn the foundations of classic French baking.

This progression-based course is perfect for anyone who loves baking, wants to develop professional techniques, or is looking to begin their pastry journey. Each class focuses on a new skill while building on what you've learned in previous weeks, making it easy to continue growing as a baker.

Week 1 – French Macarons

Take on one of France's most famous pastries with confidence. Learn how to create smooth macaron shells, perfect feet, balanced fillings, and troubleshoot common problems so you can recreate them successfully at home.

Week 2 – Choux Pastry

Master the fundamentals of pâte à choux as you learn to mix, pipe, bake, fill, and finish classic French favourites including profiteroles and éclairs. You'll also learn how to make silky pastry cream and achieve perfectly crisp shells.

Week 3 – French Tarts

Discover the secrets to beautiful French tarts by learning sweet pastry dough, blind baking, creamy fillings, fruit finishing, and professional presentation techniques.

Week 4 – Mille-Feuille

Complete the course by creating the elegant Mille-Feuille. Learn how to work with puff pastry, prepare rich vanilla crème pâtissière, assemble delicate layers, and finish with a professional glaze.

What's Included
Four hands-on classes
Step-by-step instructions from professional pastry chefs
All ingredients and equipment are provided
Recipe booklet to take home
Your creations to enjoy and share
Small class sizes for personalised guidance

Who is this course for?

This course is ideal for complete beginners and enthusiastic home bakers. No previous baking experience is required—just bring your enthusiasm and a love of French pastries.

By the end of the four weeks, you'll have mastered a range of foundational pastry techniques and be ready to continue into our future intermediate pastry workshops.

Spaces are limited to ensure every participant receives plenty of individual guidance. Early booking is recommended.

We will be running 2 starts for this course:
Dates for course:
First course: September 5th, 12th, 19th and 26th
Second course: November 7th, 14th, 21st and 28th

name: Ngā Mokopuna Tour
venue: Te Herenga Waka Marae, 46 Kelburn Parade, Wellington
long_description:
Ngā Mokopuna: A Living Building Story Tour

Join us for an introductory guided tour of Ngā Mokopuna, Te Herenga Waka Victoria University of Wellington's pioneering regenerative building project.

This experience explores the vision, values, and aspirations behind a building designed to tread lightly on the environment while creating lasting benefits for people and place. Grounded in principles of kaitiakitanga and inspired by mātauranga Māori, Ngā Mokopuna reflects a commitment to caring for our natural world and future generations.

During the tour, you'll learn about the Living Building Challenge, one of the world's most ambitious sustainability frameworks, and discover how Ngā Mokopuna has been designed to meet its rigorous standards. The project represents a significant step towards becoming one of Aotearoa New Zealand's next recognised Living Buildings.

From outside the building and surrounding precinct, you'll hear the stories behind its design, sustainability features, and cultural foundations. You'll also meet staff and student ambassadors who work and study within Ngā Mokopuna and learn firsthand how the building supports teaching, learning, wellbeing, and community.

This experience explores the vision, values, and aspirations behind a building designed to tread lightly on the environment while creating lasting benefits for people and place.
Grounded in principles of kaitiakitanga and inspired by mātauranga Māori, Ngā Mokopuna reflects a commitment to caring for our natural world and future generations.
During the tour, you'll learn about the Living Building Challenge, one of the world's most ambitious sustainability frameworks, and discover how Ngā Mokopuna has been designed to meet its rigorous standards.

long_description:
Whether you’re already retired, or planning ahead, this practical workshop will help you to reflect, re-envision and re-vitalise your life and develop a plan for your future, on your own terms. (NZ citizens and residents free with ID, all others pay $109).

In your middle years, working, retired or somewhere in between? What’s next? Life is about much more than work or leisure, but most of us have given little thought to what “retirement” might mean.

It’s difficult to speculate what may happen in the future, but we can be proactive and take control.
This course offers insights into how to make the most of our time once we’re less focused on career and/or child-rearing. It covers many of the issues people face when considering a move from current employment to a different lifestyle that includes more time to do the things we’ve always promised ourselves we’d do – “when we retire”.

After the workshop, you’ll be able to identify a number of common issues and potential ways to manage them when considering and planning your “rejuvenation”, rather than a retirement. We won’t cover financial planning, but will focus on some of the personal growth opportunities for living and making a conscious contribution to your community.

By the end of the day, you’ll have:
- Developed your own perspective on ageing and retirement in the 21st Century and identified what’s important to you
- Completed a personal life audit exercise and considered your strengths
- Explored possibilities in the major aspects of your life and identified potential challenges and strategies for overcoming them
- Developed a blueprint to maximise the best years of your life and developed a “future-proofing” downsizing plan
- Considered options to include a sense of purpose and explored and implemented choices that provide you with that sense of purpose
Bring a pen and paper.

long_description:
Bypass the mental loops and discover a new language for healing. Join us for a one-day creative journey to quiet the mind, release stress, and unlock a powerful pathway to self-compassion—no art experience required. (NZ citizens and residents free with ID, all others pay $120).

Art Therapy for Well-Being: A Canvas for Self-Discovery

This course is free for NZ citizens and residents. Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.

If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.

Sometimes, our minds get stuck in habitual thought loops—endlessly cycling through the same worries, fears, and anxieties without ever finding a breakthrough. When words fall short, art therapy offers a different language. By shifting from thinking to creating, we bypass the noise of everyday stress and tap into an intuitive visual language that can surprise us with fresh insights, new perspectives, and profound meaning.

This workshop is a gentle, immersive introduction to a pathway of self-restoration, self-compassion, and self-worth—the vital foundations for true self-healing.

What you will experience:

A Shift in Perspective: Break free from repetitive thinking by engaging the creative, intuitive side of your brain.
Tools for Daily Coping: Learn how the simple act of making art can become a sanctuary for processing stress and finding grounding.
A Pathway to Wholeness: Explore how visual expression can reveal hidden strengths and foster a deeper sense of self-care.
Important Note: You do absolutely not need to be an artist or have any artistic experience to attend. This day is about the process of expression, not the final product. While this workshop is not a substitute for clinical individual or group therapy, it is a powerful, supportive introduction to the healing power of the arts.

What to Bring:

A journal and a pen or pencil. All other creative materials will be provided. Tea and coffee provided, please bring your lunch and snacks and photo ID.

Note: Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. venue: The Library, 1/53 Courtenay Place, Te Aro, Wellington
long_description:
We return to Africa for our September book: Doris Lessing's first novel The Grass is Singing, which takes place in Southern Rhodesia (now Zimbabwe) in the 1940s. The novel opens with a newspaper clipping about the death of Mary Turner, a white woman, killed by her black servant, Moses. The bulk of the novel is the story of Mary's life and the divided society she lived in.

Lessing was born in Persia, to British parents, and moved to Southern Rhodesia when she was six. Many of her books are set in Africa. In 1949 she left the continent and arrived in London with her son Peter (leaving behind her two older children) and the manuscript for this novel under her arm. The Grass is Singing was published the following year. Lessing was awarded the Nobel Prize in literature in 2007.

This is a shorter book, fitting neatly between The Last of the Mohicans and W. Somerset Maugham's Of Human Bondage, which are both longer works. (Of Human Bondage was originally published in two volumes.) But The Grass is Singing packs a punch. Indeed, one Goodreads review begins: "Doris Lessing's first novel has the precision of a fine short story and the depth of a longer novel."

Do you keep meaning to read more of the great classics? At Wellington Classic Literature Club, we read works that have stood the test of time, whether they were written in 1780, 1880 or even 1980. We meet on the first Tuesday of the month.

If you've signed up, but things change and you're not going to be able to make it along, please email classiclitwgtn@gmail.com as we may be able to make more spaces available for others.

VENUE
We meet in the ‘Games Room’, The Library bar's private area overlooking Courtenay Place. After you enter the bar, head to your right (up the step) and through a smaller space with booths to the large carpeted space beyond (behind the big wooden sliding door).

Wellington Classic Literature Club has been running for more than a decade - since the start of 2013 - and we have a great bunch of regulars as well as readers who join us for particular books or simply when it suits.

name: A Voyage to the Moon by Offenbach: A NZSM Opera Production
venue: Adam Concert Room, NZSM Kelburn Campus, Victoria University, Gate 7, Kelburn Parade, Wellington
long_description:
Classical Performance students from the New Zealand School of Music – Te Kōkī present four performances of Jacques Offenbach's delightful comic opera A Voyage to the Moon, directed by Sara Brodie with musical direction by Kathryn Mosley.

Inspired by this year's space exploration milestones, including NASA's Artemis II mission, this production celebrates Offenbach's imaginative 1875 opera, which was a sensation in Paris, running for an impressive 185 consecutive performances during its first run.

Loosely based on Jules Verne's novel From the Earth to the Moon, A Voyage to the Moon takes audiences on a adventure filled with fantastical lunar landscapes, eccentric characters, and Offenbach's trademark comedic twists. The story follows King V'lan, his adventurous son Prince Caprice, and their companions—including Microscope and Rhombus—as they journey to the Moon, where they encounter Cosmos, Princess Fantasia, Flamma, and other curious inhabitants of the lunar world.

Directed by Sara Brodie, who also led last year's fantastic production of L'enfant et les sortilèges, the opera features vocal numbers performed in French with English surtitles. The spoken dialogue is presented in English, bringing the comedy vividly to life for contemporary audiences.

This production showcases the talents of students across the Classical Performance programme, with NZSM voice students performing all roles and in ensembles, and the NZSM piano students taking part as rehearsal pianists (répétiteurs) and playing for the performances. Musical direction is provided by Head of Collaborative Piano Kathryn Mosley, and the production is coordinated by Head of Classical Voice Jenny Wollerman.

Join us for an imaginative, entertaining, and truly 'out there' operatic adventure!

venue: Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington
long_description:
Coptic binding is one of the earliest forms of creating a book, with raw simplicity you can produce a book of any size with the unique feature of opening out flat. No special tools or materials are needed and yet a wide spectrum of creative results can be created, from a notebook, sketch book and album to a highly crafted artwork. The books themselves can be made from found items, recycled material or quality art papers and card.

In this workshop you will be guided in assembling your chosen materials for your book, create decorative covers and learn Coptic binding - an elegant and simple binding that is unlimited in versatility. You will produce one bound book and one bound album. Once you have Coptic binding in your skill set you can produce your choice of books in any shape or form, for any purpose.

All basic materials supplied.

Half an hour for lunch. Bring a drink bottle and a packed lunch to enjoy in the historic Inverlochy House or explore the cafes in Te Aro. Coffee & tea provided at lunch.

You must be at least 16 years of age to attend this course or attend with a paying adult.

id: Natural Textured Rings - Taster Class-Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki-Event Finder
name: Natural Textured Rings - Taster Class
venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
long_description:
Craft a beautiful, personalised ring - a perfect treat for yourself or a thoughtful gift for someone special! This three-hour taster class is designed for absolute beginners, though all skill levels are welcome to join the fun.

You will be guided step-by-step through the core techniques of silversmithing. You'll start by practicing basic texturing, cutting, and shaping with traditional jewellery tools using copper or brass. Once you’re comfortable, you'll move on to crafting your final piece in sterling silver.

In this hands-on workshop, you will learn to:
Measure your finger and cut the metal strip to the perfect length.
Create unique surface textures using a rolling mill, hammers, punches, and even natural elements like feathers or leaves. You can stamp names, dates, whatever you like.
Work safely with a jeweler's torch for heating and soldering the metal.
Finish your ring with sanding and polishing techniques.
By the end of the class, your beautiful, custom-made sterling silver ring will be ready to wear.

This is an ideal activity for individuals, groups of friends, or visitors to Ōtaki looking for a creative experience.

What's Included:
All practice materials (copper or brass).
A strip of sterling silver for your final ring.
All necessary consumables (sandpaper, solder, chemicals).
Use of all tools and equipment.

Important Note for Young Makers: Kids aged 12 and over are welcome to attend, but anyone under the age of 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver. Extra metals are available for purchase in the studio.
